title: How sugar affects the brain - Nicole Avena
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】糖如何影響大腦 - Nicole Avena（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Picture warm, gooey cookies, crunchy candies, velvety cakes,
cues.en: Picture warm, gooey cookies, crunchy candies, velvety cakes,
cues.zh: 想像一個溫熱、黏膩的餅乾 爽脆的糖果 細緻可口的蛋糕

cues.text: waffle cones piled high with ice cream.
cues.en: waffle cones piled high with ice cream.
cues.zh: 甜筒上堆起的冰淇淋球

cues.text: Is your mouth watering?
cues.en: Is your mouth watering?
cues.zh: 甜筒上堆起的冰淇淋球 讓你口水直流了嗎？

cues.text: Are you craving dessert?
cues.en: Are you craving dessert?
cues.zh: 讓你想吃點心了嗎？ 為什麼？

cues.text: Why?
cues.en: Why?
cues.zh: 為什麼？ 是什麼讓你的腦子

cues.text: What happens in the brain that makes sugary foods so hard to resist?
cues.en: What happens in the brain that makes sugary foods so hard to resist?
cues.zh: 是什麼讓你的腦子 無法抗拒含糖食物呢？

cues.text: Sugar is a general term used to describe a class of molecules called carbohydrates,
cues.en: Sugar is a general term used to describe a class of molecules called carbohydrates,
cues.zh: 糖是對 碳水化合物分子的 總稱

cues.text: and it's found in a wide variety of food and drink.
cues.en: and it's found in a wide variety of food and drink.
cues.zh: 而它們存在許多食物、飲料中

cues.text: Just check the labels on sweet products you buy.
cues.en: Just check the labels on sweet products you buy.
cues.zh: 只要看看你買甜食上的標簽 葡萄糖

cues.text: Glucose, fructose, sucrose, maltose, lactose, dextrose, and starch
cues.en: Glucose, fructose, sucrose, maltose, lactose, dextrose, and starch
cues.zh: 葡萄糖 果糖 蔗糖 麥芽糖 乳糖 右旋糖 和澱粉 都是不同形態的糖類

cues.text: are all forms of sugar.
cues.en: are all forms of sugar.
cues.zh: 和澱粉 都是不同形態的糖類 果糖含量高的糖漿

cues.text: So are high-fructose corn syrup, fruit juice, raw sugar, and honey.
cues.en: So are high-fructose corn syrup, fruit juice, raw sugar, and honey.
cues.zh: 果糖含量高的糖漿 果汁 粗糖 和蜂蜜

cues.text: And sugar isn't just in candies and desserts, it's also added to tomato sauce,
cues.en: And sugar isn't just in candies and desserts, it's also added to tomato sauce,
cues.zh: 而且糖類不只在糖果、點心中 它也被加到番茄醬 優格

cues.text: yogurt, dried fruit, flavored waters, or granola bars.
cues.en: yogurt, dried fruit, flavored waters, or granola bars.
cues.zh: 優格 果乾 調味水 和燕麥棒中

cues.text: Since sugar is everywhere, it's important to understand how it affects the brain.
cues.en: Since sugar is everywhere, it's important to understand how it affects the brain.
cues.zh: 既然糖類無所不在 我們更要了解 糖對大腦的影響

cues.text: What happens when sugar hits your tongue?
cues.en: What happens when sugar hits your tongue?
cues.zh: 當糖沾上舌頭時 會造成什麼反應呢？

cues.text: And does eating a little bit of sugar make you crave more?
cues.en: And does eating a little bit of sugar make you crave more?
cues.zh: 當糖沾上舌頭時 會造成什麼反應呢？ 吃一點點糖 會不會讓你想吃更多？

cues.text: You take a bite of cereal.
cues.en: You take a bite of cereal.
cues.zh: 你吃一點麥片 其中所含的糖

cues.text: The sugars it contains activate the sweet-taste receptors, part of the taste buds on the tongue.
cues.en: The sugars it contains activate the sweet-taste receptors, part of the taste buds on the tongue.
cues.zh: 其中所含的糖 刺激了舌頭味蕾上的 甜味受器

cues.text: These receptors send a signal up to the brain stem, and from there, it forks off into many areas of the forebrain,
cues.en: These receptors send a signal up to the brain stem, and from there, it forks off into many areas of the forebrain,
cues.zh: 受器向大腦傳送訊號 在那訊號分支傳送到 前腦中的不同區域

cues.text: one of which is the cerebral cortex.
cues.en: one of which is the cerebral cortex.
cues.zh: 前腦中的不同區域 其中一個就是大腦皮層

cues.text: Different sections of the cerebral cortex process different tastes:
cues.en: Different sections of the cerebral cortex process different tastes:
cues.zh: 其中一個就是大腦皮層 大腦皮層中的不同分割槽 處理不同味覺訊號 苦味

cues.text: bitter, salty, umami, and, in our case, sweet.
cues.en: bitter, salty, umami, and, in our case, sweet.
cues.zh: 苦味 鹹味 鮮味 和我們討論的甜味

cues.text: From here, the signal activates the brain's reward system.
cues.en: From here, the signal activates the brain's reward system.
cues.zh: 和我們討論的甜味 訊號在這裡活化 大腦的報償系統

cues.text: This reward system is a series of electrical and chemical pathways
cues.en: This reward system is a series of electrical and chemical pathways
cues.zh: 這個報償系統是一系列 電子與化學的傳遞鏈

cues.text: across several different regions of the brain.
cues.en: across several different regions of the brain.
cues.zh: 電子與化學的傳遞鏈 橫跨大腦不同區域

cues.text: It's a complicated network, but it helps answer a single, subconscious question:
cues.en: It's a complicated network, but it helps answer a single, subconscious question:
cues.zh: 它是一個複雜的網路 但是它可以回答一個簡單 潛意識裡的問題 我要重複這個動作嗎？

cues.text: should I do that again?
cues.en: should I do that again?
cues.zh: 我要重複這個動作嗎？

cues.text: That warm, fuzzy feeling you get when you taste Grandma's chocolate cake?
cues.en: That warm, fuzzy feeling you get when you taste Grandma's chocolate cake?
cues.zh: 在品嘗奶奶巧克力蛋糕食 你這種溫暖、放鬆的感覺

cues.text: That's your reward system saying, "Mmm, yes!" And it's not just activated by food.
cues.en: That's your reward system saying, "Mmm, yes!" And it's not just activated by food.
cues.zh: 你這種溫暖、放鬆的感覺 這就是你的報償系統說： 「我還要！」 而且它不只可由食物啟動 社交

cues.text: Socializing, sexual behavior, and drugs are just a few examples of things and experiences
cues.en: Socializing, sexual behavior, and drugs are just a few examples of things and experiences
cues.zh: 社交 性行為 和藥物 只是其中幾件 事情或經驗 可以啟動報償系統的例子

cues.text: that also activate the reward system.
cues.en: that also activate the reward system.
cues.zh: 可以啟動報償系統的例子 但是過度活化報償系統

cues.text: But overactivating this reward system kickstarts a series of unfortunate events:
cues.en: But overactivating this reward system kickstarts a series of unfortunate events:
cues.zh: 但是過度活化報償系統 會造成許多不良後果： 失控

cues.text: loss of control, craving, and increased tolerance to sugar.
cues.en: loss of control, craving, and increased tolerance to sugar.
cues.zh: 失控 渴望 和對糖類耐受性增加

cues.text: Let's get back to our bite of cereal.
cues.en: Let's get back to our bite of cereal.
cues.zh: 讓我們回到剛所講的麥片 它向下進入到你的胃

cues.text: It travels down into your stomach and eventually into your gut.
cues.en: It travels down into your stomach and eventually into your gut.
cues.zh: 它向下進入到你的胃 再到達你的腸子

cues.text: And guess what?
cues.en: And guess what?
cues.zh: 再到達你的腸子 誰料的到呢？

cues.text: There are sugar receptors here, too.
cues.en: There are sugar receptors here, too.
cues.zh: 腸子也有糖類受器

cues.text: They are not taste buds, but they do send signals telling your brain that you're full
cues.en: They are not taste buds, but they do send signals telling your brain that you're full
cues.zh: 它們不是味蕾 但也能傳送訊號 告訴你的腦說 你已經吃飽了

cues.text: or that your body should produce more insulin to deal with the extra sugar you're eating.
cues.en: or that your body should produce more insulin to deal with the extra sugar you're eating.
cues.zh: 或告訴身體需要製造更多胰島素 去處理你多吃的糖

cues.text: The major currency of our reward system is dopamine, an important chemical or neurotransmitter.
cues.en: The major currency of our reward system is dopamine, an important chemical or neurotransmitter.
cues.zh: 報償系統中的 主要貨幣是多巴胺 它是重要的神經傳導物質

cues.text: There are many dopamine receptors in the forebrain, but they're not evenly distributed.
cues.en: There are many dopamine receptors in the forebrain, but they're not evenly distributed.
cues.zh: 它是重要的神經傳導物質 前腦中有很多多巴胺受體 但是分佈並不平均

cues.text: Certain areas contain dense clusters of receptors, and these dopamine hot spots are a part of our reward system.
cues.en: Certain areas contain dense clusters of receptors, and these dopamine hot spots are a part of our reward system.
cues.zh: 特定地方有密集、叢聚的受體 這些是多巴胺的熱點 也是報償系統的一部份

cues.text: Drugs like alcohol, nicotine, or heroin send dopamine into overdrive,
cues.en: Drugs like alcohol, nicotine, or heroin send dopamine into overdrive,
cues.zh: 藥物像是酒精 尼古丁 或海洛因 會造成多巴胺受體超載

cues.text: leading some people to constantly seek that high, in other words, to be addicted.
cues.en: leading some people to constantly seek that high, in other words, to be addicted.
cues.zh: 造成一些人持續追求這種快感 也就是成癮

cues.text: Sugar also causes dopamine to be released, though not as violently as drugs.
cues.en: Sugar also causes dopamine to be released, though not as violently as drugs.
cues.zh: 糖經由一種較藥物和緩的機制 促成多巴胺的釋放 有些食物含糖量較低

cues.text: And sugar is rare among dopamine-inducing foods.
cues.en: And sugar is rare among dopamine-inducing foods.
cues.zh: 有些食物含糖量較低 例如：花球甘藍就沒有作用

cues.text: Broccoli, for example, has no effect, which probably explains why it's so hard to get kids to eat their veggies.
cues.en: Broccoli, for example, has no effect, which probably explains why it's so hard to get kids to eat their veggies.
cues.zh: 例如：花球甘藍就沒有作用 這或許可以解釋 為什麼很難叫小孩吃青菜

cues.text: Speaking of healthy foods, let's say you're hungry and decide to eat a balanced meal.
cues.en: Speaking of healthy foods, let's say you're hungry and decide to eat a balanced meal.
cues.zh: 說到健康食物 假設你餓了 而且決定要吃一餐 你這麼做後 多巴胺量激增

cues.text: You do, and dopamine levels spike in the reward system hot spots.
cues.en: You do, and dopamine levels spike in the reward system hot spots.
cues.zh: 你這麼做後 多巴胺量激增 刺激報償系統的熱點

cues.text: But if you eat that same dish many days in a row, dopamine levels will spike less and less, eventually leveling out.
cues.en: But if you eat that same dish many days in a row, dopamine levels will spike less and less, eventually leveling out.
cues.zh: 但如果你一再吃同一道菜 多巴胺量會越來越低 最後和平常無異

cues.text: That's because when it comes to food, the brain evolved to pay special attention to new or different tastes.
cues.en: That's because when it comes to food, the brain evolved to pay special attention to new or different tastes.
cues.zh: 因為當刺激來自食物時 大腦演化出特別的機制 關注新、或不同的味道

cues.text: Why?
cues.en: Why?
cues.zh: 為什麼呢？ 有兩個原因

cues.text: Two reasons: first, to detect food that's gone bad.
cues.en: Two reasons: first, to detect food that's gone bad.
cues.zh: 有兩個原因 一、確定食物是否過期 二、因為如果我們的

cues.text: And second, because the more variety we have in our diet, the more likely we are to get all the nutrients we need.
cues.en: And second, because the more variety we have in our diet, the more likely we are to get all the nutrients we need.
cues.zh: 二、因為如果我們的 飲食越多樣化 我們就更有可能 得到所有所需營養

cues.text: To keep that variety up, we need to be able to recognize a new food,
cues.en: To keep that variety up, we need to be able to recognize a new food,
cues.zh: 為了保持多樣性 我們需要辨別新食物的能力

cues.text: and more importantly, we need to want to keep eating new foods.
cues.en: and more importantly, we need to want to keep eating new foods.
cues.zh: 我們需要辨別新食物的能力 更重要的是 我們必須想吃新食物

cues.text: And that's why the dopamine levels off when a food becomes boring.
cues.en: And that's why the dopamine levels off when a food becomes boring.
cues.zh: 我們必須想吃新食物 這就是為什麼食物相同時 多巴胺變化就不明顯

cues.text: Now, back to that meal.
cues.en: Now, back to that meal.
cues.zh: 回到我們所說的那一餐

cues.text: What happens if in place of the healthy, balanced dish, you eat sugar-rich food instead?
cues.en: What happens if in place of the healthy, balanced dish, you eat sugar-rich food instead?
cues.zh: 如果將健康、平衡的飲食 以高糖份的食物代替 會發生什麼事呢？

cues.text: If you rarely eat sugar or don't eat much at a time, the effect is similar to that of the balanced meal.
cues.en: If you rarely eat sugar or don't eat much at a time, the effect is similar to that of the balanced meal.
cues.zh: 如果你很少吃糖 或一次吃的不多 它的影響與均衡飲食相同

cues.text: But if you eat too much, the dopamine response does not level out.
cues.en: But if you eat too much, the dopamine response does not level out.
cues.zh: 它的影響與均衡飲食相同 如果你吃過量 多巴胺改變並不會逐漸下降

cues.text: In other words, eating lots of sugar will continue to feel rewarding.
cues.en: In other words, eating lots of sugar will continue to feel rewarding.
cues.zh: 換句話說，吃大量的糖 會繼續使人 有被回饋的感覺

cues.text: In this way, sugar behaves a little bit like a drug.
cues.en: In this way, sugar behaves a little bit like a drug.
cues.zh: 這麼說來，糖就像毒品一樣

cues.text: It's one reason people seem to be hooked on sugary foods.
cues.en: It's one reason people seem to be hooked on sugary foods.
cues.zh: 這麼說來，糖就像毒品一樣 這是為什麼有人會對 高糖食物成癮的原因

cues.text: So, think back to all those different kinds of sugar.
cues.en: So, think back to all those different kinds of sugar.
cues.zh: 高糖食物成癮的原因 想想各種不同的糖 每種都各有不同

cues.text: Each one is unique, but every time any sugar is consumed, it kickstarts a domino effect in the brain that sparks a rewarding feeling.
cues.en: Each one is unique, but every time any sugar is consumed, it kickstarts a domino effect in the brain that sparks a rewarding feeling.
cues.zh: 每種都各有不同 但是吃進不同的糖 都會刺激腦中的多巴胺釋放 造成被回饋的感覺

cues.text: Too much, too often, and things can go into overdrive.
cues.en: Too much, too often, and things can go into overdrive.
cues.zh: 吃太多或太頻繁 都會造成超載

cues.text: So, yes, overconsumption of sugar can have addictive effects on the brain,
cues.en: So, yes, overconsumption of sugar can have addictive effects on the brain,
cues.zh: 所以過量攝取糖類 也會造成大腦的成癮

cues.text: but a wedge of cake once in a while won't hurt you.
cues.en: but a wedge of cake once in a while won't hurt you.
cues.zh: 但是偶而吃塊蛋糕無傷大雅
